Position ~15.5%, a touch over the nominal 15% target but within the trim tolerance band -- watch for sizing drift, no action needed today.

HOLD: thesis intact and reinforced. A 9/16 report describes Duolingo folding former "Max" AI features (video calls, mistake-explanations) directly into the base Super tier as AI inference costs fall -- consistent with the 9/14 Motley Fool framing of the shift away from the legacy paid tier as a positive long-term monetization move, and with CEO von Ahn's 100M-DAU-by-2028 commentary from the 9/9 Citi conference. The persistent earnings-decline flag continues to reflect deliberate AI-feature reinvestment, not demand weakness. Position ~14.75% of portfolio, just under the 15% cap -- hold, don't add; any further appreciation may force a mechanical trim on sizing alone.

HOLD: one new item to monitor, not thesis-breaking -- CNBC/Insurance Journal (9/15-16) reported AWS still cannot restore its Bahrain data center and one UAE availability zone, with the Bahrain infrastructure damage (from March Iran-related strikes) possibly unrecoverable and no update expected before early 2027. This is a regional reliability/reputational issue, not a broad US AWS outage; no revenue/customer-impact disclosure yet. Thesis otherwise intact -- watch for a follow-up disclosure.

Trimmed 30% (0.5772 sh) to de-risk given the fresh breach, keeping the bulk of the position since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.

BUY: AST SpaceMobile sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (direct-to-cell satellite connectivity). Shifting from proof-of-concept to commercial activation: BlueBird 11-13 satellites deployed, a new New Zealand gateway opened, deepening integration tests with Vodafone/Orange/Telefonica/Deutsche Telekom via a gateway JV, and US Mobile preparing a direct-to-cell launch. 2026 revenue guided to $150-200M off a near-zero base (drove the screen's outsized revenue-growth score), backed by a $1.3B backlog and over $3.7B cash on hand -- funds the capital-intensive buildout without near-term dilution risk. Known risk: execution on an expensive, tightly-timed deployment (targets imply ~165%/yr revenue growth through 2029); stock is down modestly on the mixed reaction to the BlueBird/US Mobile news despite the bull case being intact per sell-side (~$78 fair-value estimate vs. ~$59 entry). Not opportunity-tier (market cap ~$23B). Sized to $79 (~2.0% of portfolio), the remaining room in the Technology sector cap (already ~28% of portfolio before this buy) rather than a full-size position -- funded by today's VRT trim proceeds.
